title: The Rosetta Stone was found by soldiers knocking down a wall inside a fort

cover.alt: The Rosetta Stone, a dark grey slab with a broken top, densely carved with three bands of script: hieroglyphs, Demotic and Greek.

body: In July 1799 French soldiers demolishing a wall inside Fort Julien, near Rashid (Rosetta) in the Nile Delta, found a slab of dark granodiorite that had been reused as building material. It was carved with three scripts: Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic and Ancient Greek. The officer Pierre-François Bouchard realised that all three carried the same text, a priestly decree of 196 BC honouring the young king Ptolemy V. Because scholars could read the Greek, the stone became the key that let Jean-François Champollion announce the decipherment of hieroglyphs in 1822. It is only the lower part of a taller stele, and it has been on show at the British Museum almost continuously since 1802.

slides.alt: The left and right edges of the Rosetta Stone, showing faded white painted lettering on the rough grey sides.
slides.caption: The painted edges read ‘Captured in Egypt by the British Army in 1801’ and ‘Presented by King George III’. They were added by the end of 1802 and are now much faded.

slides.heading: Which script has the most surviving lines?
slides.note: The hieroglyphic band sat at the top, where the stele is broken.
slides.explanation: Greek, at the bottom, kept 54 lines; the hieroglyphs at the top only 14. Some 14 or 15 more hieroglyphic lines are thought to be missing.

events.text: Found in a wall of Fort Julien
On display at the British Museum

left.label: Long believed
left.text: For generations it was described as black basalt. The dark colour came from a coat of carnauba wax and the chalk filling the letters, added in London.

right.label: Actually
right.text: Cleaning in 1999 removed the wax and chalk and revealed the real stone: dark grey granodiorite. The slab weighs about 760 kg.

slides.question: Why did the Greek text matter so much?
options: It was a secret code key
slides.explanation: Greek was well known, so it gave the meaning of the whole text. Matching royal names such as Ptolemy across the scripts showed that hieroglyphs could spell sounds.

slides.heading: Not unique, but essential
slides.text: Three other fragmentary copies of the same decree have since been found, along with several other multilingual Egyptian inscriptions. The decree itself ordered that a copy be set up in every temple in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Greek. Today ‘Rosetta stone’ is a byword for the clue that unlocks a whole field of knowledge.
